question: The "capability approach" as applied to the Human Development Index (HDI) has been criticized for:

options.text: Being too focused on economic factors.
Being difficult to operationalize and measure.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Being difficult to operationalize and measure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)**, derived from the "capability approach," focuses on key indicators of well-being such as **life expectancy, education, and income per capita**.
 
• The capability approach emphasizes assessing individuals' actual ability to achieve valuable states of being or functioning rather than just resources or outcomes.
 
• Despite its theoretical significance, the capability approach has faced criticism for being **difficult to operationalize and measure**, especially due to its reliance on qualitative data and subjective assessments.
 
• Unlike straightforward economic metrics, capabilities involve multidimensional factors such as choices, freedoms, and opportunities, which are inherently complex to quantify.
